A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemGAS. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and corresponding content can be matched despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA and retrieval experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, efficiency measurements, and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, generator experiments, controlled token-budget comparisons, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: The four memory granularities, GMM associations, inverse-entropy router, Personalized PageRank retrieval, and LLM filtering remain unchanged. Equations 1–5 and the operational prompts are retained; the new theoretical analysis does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four benchmarks and conversational QA/retrieval tasks. LoCoMo-10 becomes LoCoMo, but Appendix A retains the same ten conversations and dataset statistics. Additional experiments reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds A-Mem to Table 1 comparisons on LongMemEval-s, LoCoMo, and LongMTBench+. It is not evaluated on LongMemEval-m or retrieval metrics. LLM-Rsum is renamed RecurSum, retaining the same cited work and results.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled over-retrieval and truncation experiments, Qwen-3 8B and 1.7B generator configurations, and token, latency, and RAM measurements. Appendix D.2 specifies 8,000 and 16,000-token budgets, although Table 10 labels both groups 8,000. These are substantial extensions of evaluation design, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine router behavior against fixed granularities and optimal selection by query type, performance under equal token budgets, generator robustness, and component latency. Conversely, v1's filtering ablation disappears. Existing retriever comparisons, hyperparameter sweeps, error analysis, and case studies largely remain after relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed protocols, confidence intervals, empirical error bars, or significance tests. Temperature-zero generation remains unchanged; the new theoretical probability bounds are not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results with A-Mem scores, router comparisons, generator results, equal-budget comparisons, and resource measurements. New Qwen-3 8B and 1.7B configurations report MemGAS F1 scores of 20.57 and 16.79. Existing main MemGAS scores remain unchanged, while SeCom's LongMemEval-m BERTScore changes from 83.16 to 83.36. The filtering-ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix H introduces a sub-Gaussian separability assumption, a mis-link probability proposition, an expected-false-edge corollary, an entropy lemma, an inverse-entropy weighting proposition, and a candidate-union coverage theorem with proof sketches. v1 contains the method equations but none of these formal arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: multi-granularity memory association, adaptive entropy-based selection, and superior QA/retrieval performance across four benchmarks. The revised title and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning query-dependent granularity preferences, generator generalization, efficiency tradeoffs, and theoretical retrieval guarantees. It removes v1's limitations about generated-memory errors and scaling, and the explanation that removing filtering improves the judge score. Appendix H additionally treats graph propagation as an optional, noncontributory component.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies BLEU-4, zero-shot evaluation, and baseline-specific retrieval units, and adds a reproducibility statement describing repository instructions. These mostly clarify existing experiments. It also drops v1's operational descriptions of the GMM and PPR ablations. The code URL and substantive prompt instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to A-Mem, Mem0, MemOS, MIRIX, and Zep, and Appendix B summarizes differences among baseline memory structures. The broader positioning around cross-granularity association and adaptive selection remains intact; citation-style changes and the RecurSum rename are not new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and terminology, rewrites the ablation discussion, adds ethics and reproducibility statements, and reorganizes appendices with a contents page and grouped generalization analyses. Most existing methodological and explanatory prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, restyles diagrams and sensitivity plots, expands the main QA and ablation tables with resource columns, and adds tables for router behavior, storage, token-budget comparisons, and generators. v1's compact main-text granularity table disappears while its results remain in appendix tables; other displays are relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: A-Mem comparisons, generator tests, and equal-budget experiments strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, v2 removes the filtering ablation and substantive limitations, reducing transparency. Its new Appendix H extends a union-of-candidates coverage result to weighted retrieval without establishing that guarantee, and Table 10 conflicts with the stated token budgets. These material benefits and weaknesses prevent a reliable net judgment of overall improvement.
